A commenter said that just a year earlier Stripe wouldn't accept any crypto-related business as a customer. A client of theirs had to switch their implementation to checkout.com because of that restriction.
Complaint about Stripe's new crypto support: you can now sell NFTs using Stripe, but VOIP startups competing with RingCentral, 8x8, etc. still get their Stripe accounts cancelled.

A UK user worried that banks with restrictive crypto policies can't tell whether a Stripe payout is NFT-related. They see Stripe enabling high-risk crypto businesses like NFT marketplaces as reputational self-harm that could get existing Stripe merchants denied banking service.

A developer said that on two projects they saw a large share of card payments that were fraud or flagged as fraud once crypto was involved. In one, attempted fraud rose suddenly right after crypto elements were introduced, which made them understand why Stripe had previously refused crypto businesses.

Criticism of Stripe's USDC-on-Solana support: Solana is described as effectively centralized, with a superminority of 22 validators, and as going offline regularly. The commenter asked whether Stripe had sold its ethics by supporting crypto while failing to support legitimate businesses.
A defender of Stripe's choice of Solana said that, having used most networks, Solana has the best experience for transacting USDC.

A Stripe user called crypto payments a massive disappointment that facilitates scams and ransomware. They said it's time to move off Stripe to providers that don't accept crypto, citing Stripe banning customers and shutting down accounts for no reason.

On how fast Stripe's stablecoin payments settle: a commenter noted Stripe appears to use custodied funds at first, so transactions are effectively instant via a centralized layer. They argued Stripe should use an Ethereum L2 like Base, with ~2s blocks, rather than Solana.
A skeptic asked why use Stripe and stablecoins at all when banks can accept FedNow instant payments. They cited a 20-second SLA, up to $100k+ per transfer, and free or very low cost.

In reply, a commenter said FedNow doesn't help Stripe's many customers who can't get US bank accounts. Forex fees on credit cards are painful outside the US and wires aren't viable for most businesses, so stablecoin rails have value there.

On Stripe Crypto Payouts (USDC via Connect): paying out in USDC only gives the illusion of an instant transfer. Converting USDC back to fiat comes with restrictions, delays and fees, making it a roundabout ACH transfer for recipients who need cash to pay bills.
Counterpoint on Stripe USDC payouts: in this user's experience, Coinbase charges no fees on USDC-to-USD conversion. With its debit card, funds are usable almost instantly.

Another commenter cited Coinbase's $25 wire fee, ACH taking 3-5 business days, and transaction limits. They concluded the business case for USDC payouts over fiat banking is 'virtually nil' and 'more gimmick than function.'

Limitation of Stripe Crypto Payouts: recipients must be individuals or sole proprietors, not companies or non-profits. The commenter said they wouldn't choose a payments solution that locks them out as their company grows.

A user found Stripe's crypto payouts confusing, unsure whether customers check out with USDC or only sellers get paid out in USDC. Another explained it is a Connect feature for marketplace platforms paying their users.
